series.label: All registered deaths
series.gradeText: Same meaning as today's measure.
series.note: Deaths from every cause in the states that registered deaths that year. A state outside the registration area has no data, which is not the same as no deaths.

series.label: Diabetes
series.gradeText: Same disease or concept as today's measure; revisions of the classification move the numbers by small amounts.

series.label: Suicide
series.gradeText: Same disease or concept as today's measure; revisions of the classification move the numbers by small amounts.

series.label: Cancer and tumors
series.gradeText: Same disease or concept as today's measure; revisions of the classification move the numbers by small amounts.
series.note: The printed group includes some tumors that are not malignant. Not verified.

series.label: Influenza and pneumonia
series.gradeText: Same disease or concept as today's measure; revisions of the classification move the numbers by small amounts.
series.note: The two printed columns, influenza and pneumonia, added together for the same state and year. The 1918 pandemic shows in 1918 and 1919.

series.label: Bright's disease and nephritis
series.gradeText: Older grouping that is close to today's measure but not the same (it also holds kidney disease that followed heart disease).

series.label: Circulatory disease (as printed)
series.gradeText: No modern equivalent: shown exactly as the printed volumes grouped it, never on today's scale.
series.note: Heart disease and stroke are narrower groups; do not compare this with the heart or stroke maps.

series.label: Accidents and violence (as printed)
series.gradeText: No modern equivalent: shown exactly as the printed volumes grouped it, never on today's scale.
series.note: One combined series: falls, motor vehicle, firearm and homicide deaths cannot be split in these tables.

series.label: Tuberculosis, all forms

series.label: Infant deaths (under 1 year)
series.gradeText: Same meaning as today's measure.
series.note: Deaths before the first birthday, with live births from the same volumes. The birth registration area was smaller than the death area until 1928, so early states may show deaths but no rate.

revisionNote: The classification of causes of death was revised about 1900, 1910, 1921, 1930 and 1939. A line on the chart marks each one inside the years shown. No adjustment is applied: a change at a line can come from the new coding, not from health.

anomalies.text: The age groups add to 74,252 but the printed total is 74,282. The publisher lists Ohio's female ages in 1916 as not adding to the total.
The age groups add to 30,684 but the printed total is 30,734. The publisher lists Kentucky's male ages in 1919 as not adding to the total.
The age groups add to 47,216 but the printed total is 47,196. The publisher lists California's male ages in 1920 as not agreeing.
The age groups add to 39,370 but the printed total is 39,430. The publisher lists Indiana's female ages in 1920 as not agreeing.
The publisher lists Kentucky in 1920 as not agreeing.
The age groups add to 72,456 but the printed total is 72,454.
The age groups add to 50,235 but the printed total is 50,237. The publisher lists Massachusetts in 1935 as having causes that do not sum to the total.
The age groups add to 5,040 but the printed total is 5,066.

yearNotes.1902: In the 1902 volume the printed totals by cause and by age and sex do not agree (the publisher's note).
yearNotes.1912: Ages are not split by sex in 1912 and 1913 (not used here).
